output.brief: The overtime overrun comes mainly from the closing contract that was not renewed, not from the hiring freeze. Call-back pay rose from about $38k to $289k. Of 2,295 call-backs, 1,962 are tagged CLOSE, and all of those date from 1 April or later. None are in Summit Hill, where the closing contract continued. Summit Hill has similar vacancies but almost no overtime growth. Regular holdover overtime hours rose only 1.5%. The 3-hour minimum pays each 30–45 minute closing round as three hours, which inflates the cost. Internal Audit checked the fraud allegation against lock logs and found no evidence of padding, so disciplining R-14 and R-22 would be wrong. The Eastgate favoritism claim is unproven. The same five or six people sign up voluntarily, and the old sign-up sheets were thrown away. A blanket overtime cap risks leaving sites unlocked, because members say they will stop taking call-backs. The injury rise may be linked to overtime, but hours were never matched to claims, so that link is unproven. Next steps: restore contracted closing or re-tender it, and track call-back spend. Also review the 3-hour minimum with the union, keep the sign-up sheets from now on, and match injury claims to payroll hours. Hold off on the eleven-position exemption until the effect of these changes is clear. Confidence is high on the main driver and lower on the secondary items.
